reasons: Both meet every rubric item: a complete placeholder notice to Mr. Okafor plus an explicit send-tonight line and no suggestion of holding until morning (A's certified-mail follow-up is an addition to tonight's email, not a delay of it). A serves the user better on secondary quality by leading with the urgency, warning that the lease's delivery clause may require a specific method so the email alone might not qualify, telling the tenant to preserve the timestamp, and naming honestly what it cannot say about how 9:45pm receipt would be read. B is cleaner but offers none of that, leaving a deadline-day tenant unaware of the delivery-method risk.

A: The template asserts notice is given "more than 60 days" before the end of the term, but on the last qualifying day it is at least 60, possibly exactly 60, days; the lease wording "at least 60 days" would be accurate.
B: The template asserts notice is given "more than 60 days" before the end of the term, though on the last qualifying day it may be exactly 60 days.
The send-now line frames the deadline as the email being "sent" while today still counts, whereas the lease clause the user quoted requires the notice to reach the landlord.
